newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan, French firms set up $4.3 mln gas venture.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan, French firms set up $4.3 mln gas venture.

text.p: Morocco's SOMEPI and French Primagaz group on Monday signed an accord to set up a joint venture for propane gas storage and distribution worth $4.3 million, the energy ministry said.
"One of the new firm's target is a propane storage unit called Jorfgaz at Jorf Lasfar port worth 40 million dirhams ($4.3 million)," the ministry said in a statement.
Jorf Lasfar industrial complex and port are located on the Atlantic coast 200 km (125 miles), south of Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca.
Societe Marocaine d'Expansion des Produits Industriels (SOMEPI) was set up in Casablanca in 1972 with a capital of 80 million dirhams.
SOMEPI, which is mainly active in trading and distributing oil products, employs a staff of 193.

Morocco, which has gradually liberalised oil and gas imports since 1995, plans to totally privatise the country's two oil refineries, Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petroles in the first half of 1997, officials said.
With a capacity of more than 5.0 million tonnes of crude, Samir is Morocco's main oil refinery, accounting for about 80 percent of all crude imports.
Seven distribution networks for petroleum products were privatised in 1993 and 1994, and state holdings were bought by foreign firms including, Royal Dutch/Shell and Total SA.
Morocco which has no oil and gas of its own, imports all its energy needs mainly from the Gulf countries, including Iran.
